source: CIRCL CVE Search + GitHub Advisory OSV + CISA KEV + NIST NVD

cves.summary: SQL injection vulnerability in the Downloads module in Php-Nuke 6.x through 7.2 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL via the (1) orderby or (2) sid parameters to modules.php.
ifconfig "-arp" in SGI IRIX 6.5 through 6.5.22m does not properly disable ARP requests from being sent or received.
Unknown vulnerability in SGI IRIX 6.5 through 6.5.22m allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a certain UDP packet.

Buffer overflow in the ssl_prcert function in the SSLway filter (sslway.c) for DeleGate 8.9.2 and earlier allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a certificate with a long (1) subject or (2) issuer name field.
The Live CD in SUSE LINUX 9.1 Personal edition is configured without a password for root, which allows remote attackers to gain privileges via SSH.

Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in XMB 1.8 Final SP2 allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary script as other users via the (1) member parameter in member.php, (2) uid parameter in u2uadmin.php, (3) user parameter in editprofile.php, (4) an onmouseover event in an align tag when bbcode is allowed, or (5) img tag where bbcode is allowed.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to transfer tenant ownership via POST /sys/tenant/changeOwenUserTenant. Low-privileged attackers can supply userId and tenantId parameters to reassign any tenant's owner to a member, including themselves, and strip the legitimate owner.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to modify tenant settings by calling PUT /sys/tenant/updateApplyStatus. Low-privileged attackers can supply any tenant id to overwrite its applyStatus field, enabling or disabling tenant administrator applications across tenants.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the SysTenantController passApply handler that allows any authenticated user to approve tenant administrator applications. Attackers can file a pending application via doApplyTenantPackUser and approve it through PUT /sys/tenant/passApply to gain tenant administrator pack permissions in any tenant.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the queryUserRolesById handler of SystemApiController that lets authenticated users read any user's role codes. Low-privileged attackers can send a userId to GET /sys/api/queryUserRolesById to enumerate role assignments and identify administrator accounts.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the OssFileController queryById handler that allows low-privileged authenticated users to read object storage file records. Attackers who know a record id can request GET /sys/oss/file/queryById to obtain original file names and direct storage URLs of files uploaded by other users.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the SysTenantController deleteApply handler that allows any authenticated user to reject tenant administrator applications. Low-privileged attackers can send PUT requests with chosen tenantId, packId and userId values to delete pending applications in any tenant and notify applicants of rejection.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the queryPageList handler of OpenApiController that allows any authenticated user to list OpenAPI registry definitions. Low-privileged attackers can query GET /openapi/list to read virtual paths, internal origin URLs, IP whitelists, and header and parameter templates intended for administrators.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to remove users from tenant product packs via PUT /sys/tenant/deleteTenantPackUser. Attackers can supply arbitrary userId and packId values in the request body to remove any user from any tenant's product pack, revoking permissions such as tenant administrator access.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the getUserPermissionSet handler of SystemApiController that allows any authenticated user to read other users' permission codes. Low-privileged attackers can supply an arbitrary userId to GET /sys/api/getUserPermissionSet to retrieve the full permission set of any account, including administrators.

JeecgBoot through 3.9.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the SysCategoryController importExcel handler that allows any authenticated user to import category dictionary entries. Low-privileged attackers can upload crafted Excel workbooks to bulk insert arbitrary nodes into the system-wide sys_category dictionary, including under existing parent nodes.
The TFTP server for Red-M 1050 (Bluetooth Access Point) can not be disabled and makes it easier for remote attackers to crack the administration password via brute force methods.

The web management server for Red-M 1050 (Bluetooth Access Point) does not use session-based credentials to authenticate users, which allows attackers to connect to the server from the same IP address as a user who has already established a session.

Red-M 1050 (Bluetooth Access Point) publicizes its name, IP address, and other information in UDP packets to a broadcast address, which allows any system on the network to obtain potentially sensitive information about the Access Point device by monitoring UDP port 8887.
Sojourn search engine allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via a .. (dot dot) attack.

When a new SQL Server is registered in Enterprise Manager for Microsoft SQL Server 7.0 and the "Always prompt for login name and password" option is not set, then the Enterprise Manager uses weak encryption to store the login ID and password.
filediff in CVStrac allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via shell metacharacters in rcsinfo.

The Virtual Private Network (VPN) capability in Novell Bordermanager 3.8 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (ABEND in IKE.NLM) via a malformed IKE packet, as sent by the Striker ISAKMP Protocol Test Suite.

A vulnerability was identified in deepseek-ai deepseek-harness up to 0.1.1-rc.2. This affects the function agent of the component dsh-workflow-worker-thread. The manipulation leads to enforcement of behavioral workflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

ZDR decoding in libnfs through 6.0.2 before 7613236 has an out-of-bounds write related to lib/libnfs-zdr.c with libnfs_zdr_bytes(), libnfs_zdr_string(), and libnfs_zdr_array(). The caller-supplied maxsize value is not honored.

A security flaw has been discovered in westboy CicadasCMS up to 2431154dac8d0735e04f1fd2a3c3556668fc8dab. This impacts the function TemplateController.save of the file /system/cms/template/save of the component Backend Template Editor. The manipulation results in path traversal. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in WPExperts APIExperts Square for WooCommerce woosquare allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects APIExperts Square for WooCommerce: from n/a through 4.7.5.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in WP Desk Flexible Quantity – Measurement Price Calculator for WooCommerce flexible-quantity-measurement-price-calculator-for-woocommerce allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Flexible Quantity – Measurement Price Calculator for WooCommerce: from n/a through 2.3.23.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Planet studio PlanetStudio Payment Gateway planetstudio-payment-gateway allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects PlanetStudio Payment Gateway: from n/a through 1.3.3.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in ClikIT Infinite Uploads infinite-uploads allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects Infinite Uploads: from n/a through 3.4.1.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in WPdreams Ajax Search Lite ajax-search-lite allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Ajax Search Lite: from n/a through 4.14.5.
Ensim WEBppliance 3.0 and 3.1 allows remote attackers to read mail intended for other users by defining an alias that is the target's email address.
Oracle 9i Application Server 9.0.2 stores the web cache administrator interface password in plaintext, which allows remote attackers to gain access.

The xp_SetSQLSecurity function in Microsoft SQL Server 2000 and SQL Server Desktop Engine (MSDE) does not properly restrict the length of a buffer before calling the srv_paraminfo function in the SQL Server API for Extended Stored Procedures (XP), which allows an attacker to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary commands, aka the "Extended Stored Procedure Parameter Parsing" vulnerability.
Buffer overflow in Microsoft Phone Book Service allows local users to execute arbitrary commands, aka the "Phone Book Service Buffer Overflow" vulnerability.
The Pocsag POC32 program does not properly prevent remote users from accessing its server port, even if the option has been disabled.
StarTech (1) POP3 proxy server and (2) telnet server allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a long USER command.
HP-UX gwind program allows users to modify arbitrary files.
Bash treats any character with a value of 255 as a command separator.
Sendmail allows local users to write to a file and gain group permissions via a .forward or :include: file.
Savant web server allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via a long GET request.
Blackboard CourseInfo 4.0 stores the local and SQL administrator user names and passwords in cleartext in a registry key whose access control allows users to access the passwords.
Tnef program in Linux systems allows remote attackers to overwrite arbitrary files via TNEF encoded compressed attachments which specify absolute path names for the decompressed output.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: wake ring pollers for local task_work

With IORING_SETUP_DEFER_TASKRUN completions are queued as local work, and
only become CQEs when the submitter enters the kernel to wait for events.
For an application that finds out via poll() or epoll on the ring fd when
it is time to do that, io_uring_poll() reports EPOLLIN if local work is
pending.

That only helps if the work is there at the time of the call. When
DEFER_TASKRUN was added, io_req_local_work_add() did io_cqring_wake(),
which took care of tasks sleeping in poll() as well. Then polling got a
wait queue of its own, ->poll_wq, and the wake up in
io_req_local_work_add() was replaced by waking the submitter directly.
Since then ->poll_wq is only woken when CQEs are committed, which for
such a ring is done by the very task that is waiting to be told to:

  submitter                           completion
  poll(ring_fd)
    io_uring_poll()  // nothing yet
    schedule()
                                      io_req_local_work_add()
                                        // ->cq_wait_nr: nobody waits
  // sleeps on

Wake ->poll_wq when the first entry is put on the work list. Like for the
eventfd, that must not be done right away if the work is queued from a
wake up handler, as the chain of wake ups could get back to the wait
queue whose lock is held. Use an RCU callback in that case, with a
reference to the ring.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/napi: make stale entries time out after 60s

With dynamic tracking a NAPI id that hasn't been seen for a minute is
meant to be dropped from the list the ring busy polls. The timeout is
added to jiffies, but it is defined as 60 * SEC_CONVERSION, and
SEC_CONVERSION isn't the number of jiffies in a second. It is the
internal factor of __timespec64_to_jiffies(), HZ scaled up by
SEC_JIFFIE_SC bits. For HZ=1000 that is 1000 << 22, which puts the
timeout at about eight years. On 32-bit the multiplication overflows.

So entries are never removed, and every id that a socket of the ring
ever had keeps being polled on each wait.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: don't retry recv on uncommitted buffers

Commit 41b70df5b38b ("io_uring/net: commit partial buffers on retry")
commits ring provided buffers when a receive is going to be retried after
a partial transfer, so that another request using the same buffer group
can't be handed the memory the first one keeps receiving into. It commits
the number of bytes received so far. That does the job for a single
buffer which is consumed as a whole, but the request hangs on to all it
has mapped:

- For a buffer ring with IOU_PBUF_RING_INC only these bytes are consumed.
  The rest of the buffer stays at the head of the ring.
- For a bundle only the buffers which hold these bytes are consumed, the
  others that were peeked stay in the ring.

In both cases the next receive with that buffer group gets memory that
the retried request is still going to write to, and whoever comes last
overwrites the data of the other. What the retry fills isn't committed at
all, as the buffer list isn't known any more at that point. So the kernel
hands it out again later on, while the CQE tells the application that it
was used, and for an incremental buffer that it is done with.

The remainder can't be committed in advance: if the request ends up
receiving less, there is no way to tell the application that more was
consumed than the CQE accounts for. Complete the request with what it has
got instead of retrying it. MSG_WAITALL is no longer honoured for
receives into incremental buffers or multi buffer bundles, they can
return a short count, with the request marked as failed like for other
short MSG_WAITALL transfers.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

soc/tegra: pmc: Fix uninitialised clock rate

For legacy 32-bit Tegra devices, the warning in the
tegra_pmc_enter_suspend_mode() function is being triggered because the
early_pmc->rate variable is never configured and hence, always 0. This
issue started occurring after updating the PMC driver to create the PMC
context dynamically which causes the 'rate' to be set in the new dynamic
context, but missed updating the rate in the early PMC context.

Fix this by initialising the early_pmc->rate variable for 32-bit Tegra
devices when the rate for the PMC context is initialised.

[treding@nvidia.com: move assignment to existing #ifdef block]

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/poll: avoid retry wakeup loss when dropping ownership

If a wakeup sets IO_POLL_RETRY_FLAG between the owning task consuming
the existing instance of IO_POLL_RETRY_FLAG and the loop check
of io_poll_check_events(), then we stall on processing the request
until an unrelated wakeup comes along.

Using atomic_cmpxchg instead of atomic_sub_return to guarantee both the
count v and poll_refs are 0 and no wake-ups are missed.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/openclose: keep the lock in io_pipe_fixed()

io_pipe_fixed() installs both ends of the pipe in the fixed file table,
drops ->uring_lock, and copies the slot numbers to the application. If
that faults, it takes the lock again and removes whatever is in these
slots.

If the request is run by io-wq the lock really is dropped in between, and
the slots are visible to everybody else. By the time the error path gets
to them, they may have been closed and reused, by IORING_OP_CLOSE and a
direct open or accept, or by IORING_REGISTER_FILES_UPDATE. Then a file is
removed from the table that has nothing to do with the failed request.

Do the copy with the lock held. Faulting in user memory under
->uring_lock is fine, the registration paths do it all the time.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: correct reservation fence slots for userq per-vm BOs eviction

It fixes both the move overflow and the eviction fence add for
evicting these per-vm BOs.
